# Proposed Control Capture: GitHub Issue #40
**AI-generated by:** Alson (A.I Agent)

## Result

GitHub issue #40 was captured as R-18 (Automated bots may abuse public registration and forgot-password endpoints). By PM direction on 2026-09-10, R-18 is approved as `Open` with Dennis Arquillano as owner and exposure `3 x 4 = 12 (High)`. The source describes a control gap and possible abuse; it does not evidence that an attack has occurred.

## Source

| Field | Value |

| Title | `security: Protect Registration and Password Reset from Bot Abuse` |
| State | Open |

| Verified | 2026-09-10 |

The issue requests bot verification, layered server-side rate limiting, protection for direct endpoints, limits on downstream verification and reset email sends, and monitoring of suspicious activity. The issue prefers Cloudflare Turnstile but does not select a provider.

## Evidence Reviewed

- `application/source/app/Actions/Fortify/CreateNewUser.php`, lines 27-33: registration attempts use a five-per-minute limit keyed only by IP address.
- `application/source/config/auth.php`, lines 89-101: password-reset token generation has a 60-second broker throttle.
- `application/source/tests/Feature/Auth/PasswordResetTest.php`, lines 34-77 and 336-351: known and unknown email requests use the same response, and repeated requests send one notification in the tested case.
- A scoped application-source search found no bot-verification integration or suspicious-activity telemetry for these flows.

These controls reduce exposure but do not demonstrate the full issue acceptance criteria, including multi-signal limits, bot verification, direct-endpoint protection, downstream email caps, or abuse monitoring.

## Duplicate And Relationship Review

- R-17 (Password-recovery emails may be unavailable, reveal account existence, or expose reset credentials or tokens) overlaps the password-reset portion, but it does not cover registration abuse, bot verification, multi-signal endpoint limits, or abuse telemetry. A separate risk is warranted.
- R-16 (New participant registration alerts may be unavailable or expose more participant email data than intended) covers notification delivery and data content, not abuse of the public registration endpoint. Link it to R-18 during the next register refresh if the PM accepts the relationship.
- CHG-13 (Replace invite-only or administrator-created participant onboarding with participant self-registration and administrator approval) and ACT-20 (Implement and verify participant self-registration with configurable email verification, administrator approval, revocation, restoration, and pending or revoked access controls) already mention registration rate limiting. Their existing scope does not evidence the complete issue #40 controls.
- ACT-23 (Confirm production registration rate limiting availability and whether it is required for the proposed live bypass) is narrower and tied to the proposed email-verification bypass. It should not be treated as closure of R-18.
- The risk-register derived summary was not recalculated. It was already inconsistent with the row-level register and is tracked by ACT-57 (Reconcile the risk-register derived summary with its row-level entries before using risk counts as a performance measure).
